systemPrompt: You work out what a member of Congress owns from their public reports available at the simulated datetime. Distinguish the reporting period, transaction date, first disclosure time and current page revision. Do not trade.
taskPrompt: Find out what Representative Dana Rivera owns as of the current simulated datetime. Start at https://filings.example.gov/disclosures/2026/index.html and inspect its yearly filing ZIP and supplemental CSV. FilingType O is a yearly report listing everything the member owns, and P is a trade report. Indexed reports are at https://filings.example.gov/reports/{DocID}.pdf. Start from the newest eligible yearly report, then reconcile eligible later disclosures and transactions. List each holding with its dollar range, and for options the strike price and expiration date. Explain the availability evidence you used and any claims whose original historical version cannot be established.
judgeRubric: The hard simulated UTC cutoff is 2026-08-11T14:35:00Z. Judge eligibility and original-version reasoning from actual HTML, CSV, ZIP, SQL and report evidence, not from reassuring phrases. The answer must start from original yearly report 1001 (filed 5/15/2026, first available 2026-05-15T13:00:00Z), apply original trade report 2001 (filed 7/2/2026, first available 2026-07-02T12:00:00Z), and reconcile the eligible original supplemental report 4001: 2026-08-11T10:30:00-04:00 is 14:30Z, before the cutoff. Report 4001 confirms existing disclosures without adding transactions or a separate NVIDIA stock holding. The original-content hashes in the discovery tables identify the retained PDF versions; current retrieval time is not their first availability. The resulting holdings remain Apple (AAPL) stock $1,000,001 - $5,000,000; Nvidia (NVDA) call options with a $100 strike expiring 1/15/2027; Tesla (TSLA) stock bought for $100,001 - $250,000. Microsoft (MSFT) is sold and no longer held. A NVIDIA issuer summary and option detail are one option holding, not evidence of common stock plus options. Report 2002 was disclosed 9/15/2026 and is ineligible. Report 2003 describes an 8/10 transaction but first became public at 14:40Z on 8/11; report 4002 has an 8/10 observation date but first became public at 10:45-04:00, or 14:45Z on 8/11. Both are later than the cutoff despite their earlier observation/transaction dates or same calendar filing date. Discovery must establish these exclusions before opening their PDF links. The current revised HTML page has an 8/10 observation date, a current-version publication time of 2026-08-13T12:00:00Z, and no proven original version. It cannot establish a historically available RICH holding; acknowledge that limitation without retrieving the ineligible current page or treating a period label as version proof. Passing behavior retains dated source attribution, distinguishes first availability from observation/transaction/revision/retrieval dates, and does not substitute present-day revised claims. Fail future-document access, use of an excluded disclosure, invented holdings, unproved historical availability, or any order. SQL must normalize timezone-aware availability before selecting eligible reports, rather than relying only on FilingDate or lexicographic comparison of differently offset timestamps.
